world.headline: Trump pressures allies to secure the Strait of Hormuz
world.description: President Trump demanded NATO members, China, Japan, South Korea, France, and the UK dispatch warships to the Strait of Hormuz to reopen the world's most critical oil shipping lane, blockaded by Iran since the start of the US-Israel war on February 28, 2026. Most countries, including Germany, Greece, Australia, and the UK, declined military involvement.
world.context: Approximately one-fifth of global seaborne oil transits the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's blockade has trapped roughly 1,000 tankers, caused the largest oil supply disruption in history, and pushed Brent crude above $100 per barrel. The IEA coordinated an emergency release of 412 million barrels of oil reserves from member nations to provide short-term buffer of approximately 26 days. Allied reluctance to engage militarily exposes the limits of US influence in managing the crisis it ignited.

timeline.label: US and Israel launch coordinated strikes on Iran, initiating the war
Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to US-affiliated vessels; oil prices begin climbing sharply
IEA announces 412 million barrel emergency oil reserve release — the largest in history
Trump publicly demands allies send warships to Hormuz; major NATO partners refuse military participation

key_terms.definition: Strategic maritime chokepoint between Iran and Oman through which approximately 20% of global seaborne oil normally passes
Paris-based intergovernmental organisation that coordinated the emergency release of 412 million barrels of oil reserves from member nations
US government emergency oil stockpile; the US committed to releasing 172 million barrels as part of the IEA coordinated action
North Atlantic Treaty Organization — military alliance of 32 nations whose members largely declined Trump's request to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz

world.headline: Oil prices top $100 a barrel as Iran war disrupts Strait of Hormuz
world.description: Brent crude surged above $100 per barrel — reaching $104–105 in intraday trading — as the US-Israel war with Iran entered its third week. Iran's near-total blockade of the Strait of Hormuz caused exports from eight major Middle Eastern producers to drop more than 60% compared to February levels, creating the largest oil supply disruption in recorded history.
world.context: The Iran war has removed roughly 15 million barrels per day from global oil markets. Emergency reserve releases from IEA members cover only approximately 26 days of the shortfall. Central banks worldwide face a fresh inflationary shock, with the Federal Reserve, ECB, and Bank of Japan all reassessing their rate-cut schedules. US petrol prices surged to their highest level since October 2023, adding direct pressure on consumers.

timeline.label: US-Israel strikes on Iran begin; Brent crude was near $65/barrel before the war
Iranian drone attacks force closure of Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and world's largest LNG facility
US strikes Kharg Island military assets; Brent crosses $100/barrel for the first time since 2022
Oil hits $104; IEA emergency release provides temporary buffer but analysts warn it cannot offset Hormuz closure

key_terms.definition: International oil benchmark derived from North Sea crude; surpassed $100/barrel for the first time since 2022 during the Iran war
Iran's main oil export hub in the Persian Gulf, handling approximately 90% of Iran's crude exports; struck by US forces on March 13, 2026
Investment bank whose commodities strategist warned that a direct strike on Kharg Island oil infrastructure would trigger severe Iranian retaliation and catastrophic price spikes
US central bank reassessing its rate-cut schedule in response to fresh inflationary pressures from surging oil prices caused by the Iran war

world.headline: Gulf Arab states intercept missiles and drones as Iran threatens to widen the war
world.description: Gulf Arab states intercepted multiple waves of Iranian missiles and drones targeting regional infrastructure. Dubai International Airport, the world's busiest by passenger traffic, temporarily halted flights after a nearby drone strike sparked a fire. Debris from an intercepted Iranian drone struck a UAE oil terminal, forcing a temporary operational suspension. Saudi Arabia separately confirmed the interception of a drone in its Eastern Province.
world.context: Iran's retaliatory strikes have extended beyond the Hormuz blockade to direct attacks on Gulf energy and civilian infrastructure, broadening the conflict's geographic and economic reach. The attacks on Gulf states — which have maintained nominal neutrality — risk forcing additional regional actors into the war and further destabilising global energy and aviation markets at a moment of extreme fragility.

timeline.label: US-Israeli war on Iran begins with coordinated strikes
Iranian strikes force closure of Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and the world's largest LNG facility
Dubai International Airport suspends flights after nearby drone attack; Saudi Arabia intercepts drone in Eastern Province
Debris from intercepted Iranian drone strikes a UAE oil terminal, forcing suspension of operations

key_terms.definition: World's busiest international airport by passenger traffic, temporarily closed after a drone attack during the Iran war
Iran's elite military force responsible for missile and drone strikes targeting Gulf regional infrastructure
Bloc of Arab Gulf states — Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman — caught in the crossfire of the Iran war despite nominal neutrality

world.headline: After attacks on Iran's oil facilities, toxic black rain endangers the public
world.description: Smoke and toxic fallout from burning oil infrastructure struck by US and Israeli forces in Iran have generated widespread 'black rain' — oil-contaminated precipitation — falling on populated areas in Iran and neighbouring countries. Health authorities warned of severe risks to respiratory and skin health from prolonged exposure to hydrocarbon-laden rainfall and particulate matter.
world.context: The environmental and public health consequences of the Iran war's industrial destruction are compounding the geopolitical crisis. Black rain events carry toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and heavy metals, posing long-term cancer and neurological risks to affected populations. The phenomenon echoes the environmental catastrophe triggered by the burning of Kuwaiti oil wells during the 1991 Gulf War, which caused regional public health emergencies lasting years.

timeline.label: Iraqi forces set fire to over 600 Kuwaiti oil wells during the Gulf War, generating black rain across the region for months
US-Israel war on Iran begins; US strikes on oil infrastructure ignite major fires at Iranian refineries and storage facilities
Initial reports of black rain and toxic precipitation emerge from areas downwind of burning Iranian oil infrastructure
Associated Press and WHO issue warnings about the public health emergency posed by toxic black rain affecting Iran and neighboring regions

key_terms.definition: Oil-contaminated precipitation generated when burning petroleum infrastructure sends hydrocarbons into the atmosphere, which then fall with rainfall over populated areas
Toxic chemical compounds released by burning fossil fuels; linked to cancer, respiratory disease, and neurological damage through prolonged exposure
UN health agency that issued warnings about the public health risks of toxic fallout from burning Iranian oil infrastructure

world.headline: Pentagon sees Iran war lasting up to six weeks; Trump aide confirms extended conflict timeline
world.description: The Pentagon's internal assessment projects the US-Israel war with Iran could last up to six weeks, a Trump administration aide confirmed to Bloomberg. US and Israeli officials separately indicated to CNN that fighting would continue for weeks, dimming hopes of a rapid resolution. Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi publicly declared Iran was prepared for a prolonged war.
world.context: A six-week war timeline means the global oil supply disruption could persist well beyond the IEA's 26-day emergency buffer capacity, threatening a second and more severe price shock. It also means sustained pressure on Gulf Arab economies, global inflation, Ukraine peace talks, and central bank policy. The Pentagon's estimate suggests the US has calibrated military objectives that extend beyond initial strikes — raising the stakes for diplomatic off-ramps.

timeline.label: US-Israel war on Iran begins; initial strikes target nuclear and missile infrastructure
Iran's FM Araghchi publicly declares Iran is prepared for a long war and will not negotiate under military pressure
CNN reports Trump officials and Israel signal fighting will continue for weeks
Bloomberg confirms Pentagon's internal assessment projects the war could last up to six weeks

key_terms.definition: Iran's Foreign Minister who publicly stated Iran is prepared for a prolonged war and will not negotiate under military pressure
US Department of Defense headquarters; its internal assessment projects the Iran war could last up to six weeks
The 412 million barrel emergency oil release coordinated by the IEA — enough to offset the Hormuz supply disruption for approximately 26 days

world.headline: Formula 1 calls off April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia due to Iran war
world.description: Formula 1 officially cancelled its planned April 2026 races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, citing the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran and the deteriorating security environment across the Gulf region. The cancellations affect two of the three opening races of the 2026 F1 season, forcing a significant restructuring of the calendar.
world.context: The F1 cancellations represent the first major international sporting withdrawal from the Gulf region since the Iran war began, signalling the conflict's cascading effects on commerce, tourism, and events. Bahrain and Saudi Arabia have invested billions in Formula 1 contracts as part of their economic diversification and soft power strategies. The cancellations add to the economic toll on Gulf states already facing their worst financial outlook since the 1990s on the back of reduced oil revenue and disrupted trade.

timeline.label: Saudi Arabia signs a 10-year F1 hosting contract worth approximately $650 million; Bahrain Grands Prix have been held since 2004
US-Israel war on Iran begins; Gulf security situation deteriorates rapidly
F1 teams and logistics providers flag safety concerns about travelling to the Gulf region amid escalating missile and drone strikes
Formula 1 officially announces cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix scheduled for April 2026

key_terms.definition: The world's premier single-seater motorsport competition, governed by the FIA; the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia rounds were cancelled due to the Iran war
Saudi Arabia's economic diversification strategy for which F1 hosting serves as a key soft power and tourism element; now impacted by the Iran war cancellation

world.headline: North Korea conducts test of nuclear-capable rocket launchers
world.description: North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un oversaw a live-fire test of 12 nuclear-capable 600mm KN-25 multiple rocket launchers on March 14, 2026, firing them at an island target over 360 km away in the East Sea. KCNA confirmed the test and stated the launchers successfully demonstrated their range and accuracy. South Korea had separately detected approximately 10 ballistic missile launches the previous day from the Sunan area near Pyongyang.
world.context: The test was timed to coincide with the annual US-South Korea Freedom Shield military exercise running through March 19. The KN-25 system has a range of up to 420 km and is confirmed capable of carrying the Hwasan-31 tactical nuclear warhead, placing nearly all of South Korea within reach. The launch signals that North Korea is exploiting the global distraction caused by the Iran war to escalate its nuclear deterrence posture without attracting proportionate international attention.

timeline.label: North Korea confirms the KN-25 system is capable of carrying the Hwasan-31 tactical nuclear warhead
Kim Jong Un presides over ceremony formally delivering 50 new five-tube KN-25 launchers to the Korean People's Army
South Korea detects approximately 10 ballistic missile launches from North Korea's Sunan area toward the East Sea
Kim Jong Un oversees live-fire KN-25 test; rockets hit island target 360+ km away, confirmed by KCNA

key_terms.definition: Western designation for North Korea's 600mm multiple rocket launcher system with a 380–420 km range, capable of carrying the Hwasan-31 nuclear warhead
North Korea's tactical nuclear warhead confirmed compatible with the KN-25 system, enabling sub-strategic nuclear strikes
North Korea's official state media outlet that confirmed the KN-25 live-fire test
Annual US-South Korea computer-simulated command post exercise; the 2026 edition runs March 14–19 and triggered North Korea's latest provocations
Powerful sister of Kim Jong Un who warned that the joint US-South Korea military drills could have 'unimaginably terrible consequences'

world.headline: Zelenskyy: Kyiv waiting on US and Russia for next round of Ukraine peace talks
world.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Kyiv is ready to participate in the next round of US-Ukraine-Russia peace talks but said Ukraine is waiting for Washington and Moscow to agree on a venue. Russia refused to meet on US soil; the US had not proposed an alternative location. The talks had been placed on hold since the outbreak of the US-Iran war on February 28, 2026.
world.context: The diversion of US military resources and diplomatic attention to the Iran war has stalled Ukraine-Russia negotiations that had been progressing in the UAE. Zelenskyy warned of a 'very high' risk that Iran war demand for Patriot air defence systems could drain Ukraine's stockpiles needed to counter ongoing Russian missile and drone barrages — over 1,770 drones and 86 missiles were fired at Ukraine in the single week prior. Ukraine fears being 'sidelined' as the US focuses on the Middle East.

timeline.label: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
Zelenskyy announces a new trilateral peace round is expected in Abu Dhabi in early March after talks in Geneva
US-Israel war on Iran erupts, shifting global attention away from Ukraine and placing peace talks on hold
Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine is ready to negotiate but is waiting on the US and Russia to agree on venue and timing

key_terms.definition: US Special Envoy involved in Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations
US-made air defence system deployed to protect Ukraine from Russian missile attacks; Zelenskyy warned of risk that Iran war demand could divert supplies away from Ukraine
Hungarian Prime Minister who vetoed new EU sanctions on Russia and has been a persistent obstacle to European unity on Ukraine support
European-made air defence system being explored by France as an alternative to US Patriot batteries for Ukraine

world.headline: Gulf economies at risk of worst slump since 1990s on Iran war
world.description: Bloomberg analysis warned that Gulf Arab economies face their worst economic slump since the 1990s as the US-Israel war with Iran disrupts trade, tourism, aviation, energy exports, and foreign investment. Drone and missile strikes on Gulf infrastructure, the Hormuz blockade, and the collapse of regional confidence have compounded the oil price shock. Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, and Qatar are all reassessing 2026 fiscal projections downward.
world.context: Gulf states had been on track for a strong 2026 driven by high oil prices, tourism, and Vision 2030-aligned investment. The war has reversed this trajectory in weeks. The 1990s comparison refers to the 1990–1991 Gulf War period when regional GDP contracted sharply. Today, Gulf economies are more diversified and have larger sovereign wealth funds, but their energy infrastructure and trade routes remain critically exposed to the current conflict.

timeline.label: Iraq invades Kuwait; Gulf economies suffer severe contraction through 1991 during the last comparable regional military conflict
US-Israel war on Iran begins; Gulf states enter heightened alert; tourism, aviation, and investment flows begin declining
Iranian drone and missile strikes damage Gulf energy and civilian infrastructure; Dubai airport temporarily suspends flights
Bloomberg and IMF analysts warn Gulf GDP growth could turn negative in 2026 — worst outlook since the 1991 Gulf War

key_terms.definition: Saudi Arabia's economic diversification strategy aimed at reducing dependence on oil revenue; now severely disrupted by the Iran war's economic impact
One of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds, held by the UAE government as a financial buffer against economic shocks including the current war
Economic and political bloc of six Gulf Arab states whose combined GDP and trade flows are now severely threatened by the Iran war

world.headline: World's top central banks confront fresh inflation threat as Iran war jolts oil prices
world.description: The Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, Bank of Japan, Bank of England, and other major central banks are reassessing their monetary policy paths after oil prices surged above $100 per barrel following the US-Israel attack on Iran. The oil shock threatens to reignite inflation just as central banks had been signalling rate cuts, forcing a hawkish recalibration that risks slowing global growth.
world.context: Oil at $100 adds approximately 0.7–1.2 percentage points to headline inflation in advanced economies by standard economic models. The timing is particularly damaging because it coincides with a period of fragile disinflation — the Fed had been signalling two cuts in 2026, the ECB had already begun easing, and the BOJ had just exited negative rates. A sustained oil shock could delay cuts by two to three quarters and risk stagflation if energy costs pass through to wages and core inflation.

timeline.label: Global inflation begins declining from peak levels; central banks begin signalling a shift toward rate cuts in 2025–2026
US-Israel war on Iran begins; Brent crude immediately jumps from $65 to $80/barrel within 48 hours
Brent crude crosses $100/barrel following US strikes on Kharg Island; central bank governors issue emergency assessments
Fed, ECB, BOJ, and BOE all signal rate-cut timelines may need to be pushed back due to the oil-driven inflation shock

key_terms.definition: US central bank that had been expected to cut interest rates in 2026 but is now reassessing due to oil-driven inflation from the Iran war
Central bank of the eurozone, which had begun its rate-cut cycle but now faces fresh inflation pressure from $100 oil
Japan's central bank that only recently exited negative interest rates and is now facing renewed inflationary pressure from oil prices
A simultaneous combination of stagnant economic growth and high inflation — the risk scenario central banks fear if the oil shock is sustained

national.headline: Indian-flagged LPG tanker Shivalik reaches Mundra Port after successful transit through Strait of Hormuz
national.description: The Indian-flagged LPG carrier Shivalik, operated by the Shipping Corporation of India and carrying approximately 22,000 tonnes of LPG, arrived at Mundra Port in Gujarat on March 16 after successfully crossing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz — one of two Indian-flagged tankers to receive passage following India's intensive diplomatic engagement with Tehran. A second vessel, Nanda Devi, was expected at Kandla Port on March 17.
national.context: Iran has largely blocked the Strait of Hormuz since February 28, causing a critical LPG shortage for India's 333 million households with LPG cooking connections. India secured this passage through four rounds of talks between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi. Twenty-two Indian-flagged vessels carrying 611 seafarers remained stranded in the Persian Gulf, and no blanket arrangement was yet in place — each passage required case-by-case negotiation.

timeline.label: US-Israel attacks on Iran begin; Iran closes Strait of Hormuz, trapping Indian vessels in the Persian Gulf
EAM Jaishankar holds multiple rounds of talks with Iranian FM Araghchi on maritime safety and energy security
Shivalik and Nanda Devi transit the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's ambassador to India confirms Tehran approved the passage
Shivalik docks at Mundra Port; India's Ministry of Petroleum confirms 92,700 MT of LPG is en route to address cooking gas shortage

key_terms.definition: Indian state-owned shipping company operating the Shivalik and Nanda Devi LPG tankers
State-run Indian energy company that chartered the two LPG vessels from Qatar's Ras Laffan terminal
India's External Affairs Minister who conducted four rounds of talks with Iran's FM Araghchi to secure vessel passage
Major port in Gujarat, India, designated as the unloading destination for the Shivalik LPG carrier
Liquefied Petroleum Gas — a cooking fuel used by approximately 333 million Indian households, now facing shortage due to Hormuz blockade

national.headline: MEA confirms over 2 lakh passengers returned from Gulf region as regional security situation evolves
national.description: India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that over 200,000 passengers have returned to India from Gulf countries since the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran on February 28, 2026. The returns were facilitated through coordinated diplomatic and logistical efforts as security across Gulf states deteriorated with repeated missile and drone strikes.
national.context: India has a diaspora of approximately 9 million people in Gulf countries, making it uniquely exposed to the ongoing conflict. The scale of returns — 2 lakh in under three weeks — reflects heightened anxiety among Indian workers and residents in the region. India has simultaneously pursued diplomatic exemptions for its shipping, secured safe return routes for citizens, and maintained dialogue with all conflict parties to protect its energy and labour interests while avoiding alignment with any bloc.

timeline.label: US-Israel war on Iran begins; Gulf region enters a state of heightened alert with Iranian missile and drone activity
Dubai International Airport temporarily suspends flights after nearby drone strikes, creating immediate disruption for Indian travellers
India negotiates safe passage for Indian-flagged LPG carriers through the Strait of Hormuz through diplomatic channels
MEA confirms over 2 lakh Indian nationals have returned from Gulf countries since the start of the Iran war

key_terms.definition: India's foreign ministry responsible for diplomatic engagements and consular services including citizen evacuation coordination
Approximately 9 million Indian nationals living and working across GCC countries — particularly UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait — representing one of India's largest overseas communities
The six-nation Arab Gulf bloc whose member states host the majority of the Indian diaspora now returning home due to the Iran war

national.headline: Fitch Ratings upgrades India's FY26 GDP growth forecast to 7.5% citing resilient domestic demand
national.description: Fitch Ratings raised India's GDP growth forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2026 to 7.5%, up from its December 2025 projection of 7.4%, driven by strong consumer spending estimated at 8.6% and investment growth of 6.9%. High-frequency indicators including GST collections, manufacturing output, air travel, and digital payments showed sustained momentum through February 2026.
national.context: The upgrade makes India one of the few credible bright spots in a global economy rattled by the Iran war's oil price shock. Fitch warned separately that if oil prices remain near $100 per barrel — the current scenario — it would constitute a significant adverse global supply shock threatening the FY27 outlook. India's external vulnerability through oil imports is its key risk, with every $10/barrel rise in crude adding approximately 0.4% to India's current account deficit.

timeline.label: Fitch projected India FY26 GDP at 7.4% in its December 2025 Global Economic Outlook
India's Q3 FY26 GDP growth recorded at 7.8% on rebased 2022–23 base year
US-Israel war on Iran begins; oil prices begin climbing sharply, adding inflationary risk to India's FY27 outlook
Fitch raises India FY26 forecast to 7.5% in its Global Economic Outlook — March 2026 edition

key_terms.definition: Global credit rating agency that publishes periodic macroeconomic forecasts; upgraded India's FY26 GDP forecast to 7.5% in March 2026
Indian fiscal year running from April 2025 to March 2026
India's unified indirect tax system; GST collections are a key high-frequency indicator of economic activity tracked by analysts
Chief Economist at Fitch Ratings who warned that sustained $100/barrel oil would be a significant adverse global supply shock

national.headline: India's Defence Forces Vision 2047 outlines roadmap for integrated theater commands and self-reliance
national.description: India's armed forces released a strategic document titled Defence Forces Vision 2047, outlining a roadmap for creating integrated theater commands, achieving self-reliance in defence manufacturing, and aligning military capability with India's ambition to become a developed nation by its centenary of independence in 2047.
national.context: The document arrives amid a sharply deteriorating global security environment — with the Iran war disrupting Gulf shipping and threatening Indian energy security, Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, and North Korea's nuclear escalation. India's push to accelerate military theaterisation reflects strategic lessons from the Iran crisis, where India's diplomatic influence was tested without military commitment to any bloc, underscoring the value of strategic autonomy backed by credible defence capacity.

timeline.label: India creates the post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) to begin the process of military theaterisation
India's first CDS, General Bipin Rawat, dies in a helicopter crash, temporarily slowing theaterisation plans
India announces the formal framework for joint logistics and integrated theatre commands in a phased approach
Defence Forces Vision 2047 document released, formalising the theaterisation roadmap and self-reliance targets

key_terms.definition: Joint military structures combining Army, Navy, and Air Force under a unified operational command, replacing single-service silos
India's self-reliance initiative in defence manufacturing to reduce import dependence and build indigenous capabilities
India's strategic planning framework targeting the nation's centenary of independence in 2047 as a benchmark for developed-nation status across all sectors including defence
India's top military position responsible for coordinating joint operations and theaterisation across the Army, Navy, and Air Force

national.headline: ACME Solar commissions 143 MW battery energy storage capacity in Rajasthan under Phase-I rollout
national.description: ACME Solar Holdings commissioned 143 megawatts of battery energy storage system capacity in Rajasthan, marking a significant milestone in India's Phase-I utility-scale energy storage deployment. The project stores surplus solar energy during peak generation hours and dispatches it to the grid during peak demand periods.
national.context: India has set a target of 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, and battery storage is critical for grid stability as solar and wind generation scale up. Rajasthan — India's largest state and a leading solar radiation zone — is emerging as the hub for both solar generation and storage projects. This commissioning represents one of the largest BESS deployments in India to date and signals the accelerating maturity of India's energy storage industry.

timeline.label: India announces its National Framework for Battery Energy Storage Systems with targets under the Green Energy Corridor programme
ACME Solar wins Phase-I BESS contract in Rajasthan through competitive tariff-based bidding
Construction and grid integration work begins at the Rajasthan BESS site
ACME Solar commissions 143 MW of BESS capacity in Rajasthan, achieving Phase-I rollout milestone

key_terms.definition: Large-scale battery installations that store electrical energy for grid dispatch, enabling greater integration of intermittent solar and wind power
Indian renewable energy company focused on utility-scale solar and storage projects, commissioning one of India's largest BESS projects in Rajasthan
India's transmission infrastructure programme to connect renewable energy generation zones to demand centres, supporting the 500 GW 2030 target

national.headline: Centre initiates trials for indigenous 6G technology under 'Bharat 6G Mission' in collaboration with IITs
national.description: India's government has launched formal trials of indigenous 6G wireless technology developed under the Bharat 6G Mission, in collaboration with Indian Institutes of Technology. The initiative is India's bid to contribute intellectual property and manufacturing capacity to global 6G standards rather than remain a passive adopter of foreign technology.
national.context: India is one of the last major economies to complete a full 5G rollout, making the concurrent push into 6G research a strategic statement of technological ambition. The Bharat 6G Mission aims to ensure India has IP stakes in 6G, avoiding the foreign vendor dependency that characterised its 3G, 4G, and 5G deployments. Successful indigenisation would also reduce long-term import bills, strengthen India's semiconductor value chain, and support its broader Atmanirbhar Bharat technology agenda.

timeline.label: India launches the Bharat 6G Vision document and establishes a Technology Innovation Group on 6G
India completes 5G rollout across major cities through Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel

Government initiates formal trials of indigenous 6G technology developed in collaboration with IITs

key_terms.definition: India's national programme to develop indigenous 6G wireless technology, targeting IP ownership and domestic manufacturing capacity for commercialisation around 2030
India's premier public technical universities, serving as key R&D partners in the Bharat 6G Mission
Sixth-generation wireless technology, expected to succeed 5G with speeds up to 1 Tbps and AI-native network architecture; global commercial deployment expected around 2030
India's self-reliance policy framework spanning technology, defence, manufacturing, and energy sectors

national.headline: Ministry of Shipping accords priority berthing to six LPG carriers at major ports to mitigate fuel crunch
national.description: India's Ministry of Shipping has designated six LPG carriers as priority berthing vessels at major Indian ports, allowing them to dock ahead of other vessels to speed up LPG unloading and mitigate the cooking gas shortage caused by disruptions to Gulf supply routes. The move accompanies the confirmation that 92,700 MT of LPG is en route to India.
national.context: India imports approximately 60% of its LPG from Gulf countries. The Iran war's Hormuz blockade has severely disrupted supply lines, threatening cooking gas availability for hundreds of millions of Indian households. Priority berthing reduces port turnaround time, accelerating the replenishment cycle. The measure is one of several emergency logistics steps taken alongside diplomatic negotiations for vessel passage and activation of strategic reserves.

timeline.label: US-Israel war on Iran begins; Iran blocks the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting Gulf LPG supply routes to India
India's petroleum ministry activates emergency LPG supply measures and approaches alternative suppliers
Diplomatic negotiations secure passage for two Indian LPG tankers through the Strait of Hormuz
Ministry of Shipping grants priority berthing status to six LPG carriers at major Indian ports to accelerate unloading

key_terms.definition: Port authority designation that allows designated vessels to dock ahead of other traffic, reducing turnaround time and accelerating cargo unloading
Cooking and heating fuel used by approximately 333 million Indian households; supply critically disrupted by the Hormuz blockade
Indian government ministry responsible for maritime policy, port management, and shipping regulations

national.headline: NITI Aayog sets $850 billion annual revenue target for Indian technology services sector by 2035
national.description: NITI Aayog has set an ambitious target of $850 billion in annual revenue for India's technology services sector by 2035, up from approximately $254 billion in FY25. The target encompasses software exports, IT-enabled services, and emerging AI and cloud services, and forms part of India's broader economic transformation roadmap.
national.context: India's IT services sector is currently the world's largest by export revenue, employing approximately 5.4 million people directly. The $850 billion target would require sustaining roughly 12–13% compound annual growth over the next decade, well above current trend rates of 7–10%. The target's achievement depends on India's ability to capture a significant share of global AI services demand — a rapidly expanding market in which India's engineering talent base gives it a structural advantage.

timeline.label: India's IT exports surpass $200 billion for the first time, establishing India as the dominant global IT services provider
India's IT services sector reaches approximately $254 billion in annual revenue in FY25
AI services demand begins reshaping the global IT outsourcing market, creating new growth vectors for Indian IT majors
NITI Aayog sets $850 billion annual revenue target for the Indian tech services sector by 2035

key_terms.definition: National Institution for Transforming India — India's premier public policy think tank and strategy advisory body that replaced the Planning Commission in 2015
Information Technology and Business Process Management — India's dominant export industry encompassing software development, IT-enabled services, and business process outsourcing
National Association of Software and Service Companies — India's IT industry body that tracks sector performance and advocates for growth-enabling policies

science.headline: NASA ready for Artemis II crewed Moon mission launch scheduled as early as April 1
science.description: NASA completed its Flight Readiness Review for Artemis II and is targeting a launch no earlier than April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B. The 10-day mission will carry four astronauts — Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Jeremy Hansen — on a free-return trajectory around the Moon and back to Earth, the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in December 1972.
science.context: Artemis II was originally targeting a February 2026 launch but was delayed after engineers discovered a helium flow issue in the upper stage during a wet dress rehearsal, resolved by replacing a blocked seal. The mission will verify all life support and navigation systems needed for deep space human exploration before the planned crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV. Victor Glover will become the first person of colour, and Christina Koch the first woman, to reach deep space.

timeline.label: Artemis I uncrewed mission completes lunar flyby and splashdown in the Pacific, validating the SLS/Orion stack
Artemis II integrated SLS and Orion spacecraft roll out to Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center
Wet dress rehearsal identifies helium flow issue in the upper stage; vehicle rolled back to VAB for repairs
NASA completes Flight Readiness Review and sets April 1 as target launch date after fixing the helium seal

key_terms.definition: NASA's heavy-lift rocket designed to carry the Orion spacecraft and crew beyond low Earth orbit to the Moon; Artemis II will be its second flight
NASA's deep-space crew vehicle designed to carry astronauts to the Moon and eventually Mars

NASA's Kennedy Space Center launch pad used for the Artemis programme

science.headline: Astronomers discover RBFLOAT, the brightest fast radio burst ever detected, traced to a nearby galaxy
science.description: An international team including MIT physicists detected FRB 20250316A — nicknamed RBFLOAT (Radio Brightest FLash Of All Time) — in the galaxy NGC 4141, approximately 130 million light-years away in Ursa Major. Using the CHIME telescope and its new continent-spanning Outrigger array, scientists pinpointed the burst to a region just 45 light-years across on the edge of a star-forming zone. Follow-up observations with the James Webb Space Telescope revealed an unexpected infrared signal at the burst's location.
science.context: RBFLOAT is both the brightest and one of the closest fast radio bursts ever detected, providing the clearest look yet at the environment surrounding these mysterious phenomena. The burst has not repeated — challenging models that suggest all FRBs should repeat — and hints the source may be a slightly older magnetar displaced from its birth site. The JWST infrared finding marks the first time individual stars near an FRB source have been resolved, opening a new observational frontier.

timeline.label: First fast radio burst ever discovered; over 4,000 FRBs subsequently detected, mostly unlocalized
CHIME telescope begins operations in British Columbia, detecting hundreds of FRBs per year
RBFLOAT (FRB 20250316A) detected by CHIME and immediately localised by the Outrigger array to galaxy NGC 4141
Research published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters; JWST reveals unexpected infrared signal at burst location

key_terms.definition: Extremely powerful millisecond-long flashes of radio waves from beyond our galaxy whose exact origins remain unknown

science.headline: New blood test for brain cancer achieves over 90% accuracy in detecting glioblastomas
science.description: Researchers at the University of Manchester, led by Professor Petra Hamerlik, identified two blood-borne proteins — coagulation factor IX (F9) and cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) — that together form a dual-marker signature distinguishing glioblastoma patients from healthy individuals with over 90% diagnostic accuracy. The test maintained its performance even when the cancer returned after treatment. The study was published in Neuro-oncology Advances and a clinical trial across six UK sites and four international sites has been launched.
science.context: Glioblastoma is the most common and aggressive adult brain cancer, with a median survival of 14–16 months. Current diagnosis relies on MRI scans and invasive surgical biopsies, which cannot be repeated frequently and often miss early recurrence. A reliable blood test would enable earlier diagnosis, real-time treatment monitoring, and reduced need for invasive procedures — potentially improving survival outcomes for the approximately 300,000 people diagnosed with glioblastoma annually worldwide.

science.headline: Researchers identify TDP43 protein as critical link between DNA repair, ALS, and dementia
science.description: Researchers at Houston Methodist discovered that TDP43 — a protein already known to be involved in ALS and frontotemporal dementia — is a critical regulator of the DNA mismatch repair system. When TDP43 levels are too high or too low, mismatch repair genes become hyperactive, damaging neurons and destabilising the genome. Analysis of cancer databases additionally found higher TDP43 levels correlated with increased mutation loads in tumours, placing the protein at the intersection of neurodegeneration and cancer biology. The study was published in Nucleic Acids Research.
science.context: TDP43 is misregulated in over 97% of ALS cases and approximately 45% of frontotemporal dementia cases. The discovery that it also controls DNA mismatch repair — one of the most fundamental cellular processes — radically expands its disease relevance and opens new therapeutic pathways. In laboratory models, reducing the excessive DNA repair activity caused by abnormal TDP43 partially reversed cellular damage, suggesting a potential treatment strategy for both ALS and cancer.

science.headline: Meta signs $27 billion five-year deal with Nebius for AI computing capacity
science.description: Meta Platforms signed a landmark five-year agreement with Amsterdam-based Nebius Group worth up to $27 billion for AI computing infrastructure. The deal provides $12 billion of dedicated capacity starting early 2027, built on one of the first large-scale deployments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. Meta also committed to purchase up to an additional $15 billion of available Nebius compute capacity over the same five-year period. Nebius shares surged 14% on the announcement.
science.context: The deal is one of the largest external compute contracts in the history of the technology industry and signals a fundamental shift in how hyperscalers secure AI infrastructure. Meta is planning capital expenditure of up to $135 billion on AI in 2026. Big Tech giants are increasingly supplementing their own data centre build-outs by locking in GPU and power capacity from specialised neocloud providers like Nebius — a market dynamic accelerated by global DRAM and GPU shortages driven by AI demand. This also marks the first large-scale commercial deployment of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin AI chip architecture.

science.headline: Micron completes $1.8 billion acquisition of PSMC site in Taiwan to boost AI memory production
science.description: Micron Technology completed the acquisition of Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation's P5 fabrication site in Tongluo, Miaoli County, Taiwan for $1.8 billion on March 15, 2026. The site includes approximately 300,000 square feet of existing 300mm cleanroom space and will be retrofitted for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory production. Micron also plans a second facility of comparable scale at the same site, with construction starting by fiscal year-end 2026.
science.context: The acquisition directly addresses a global DRAM supply squeeze in which data centres are projected to consume 70% of all memory chips produced in 2026. HBM is the critical memory type powering AI training and inference, and Micron trails SK Hynix and Samsung in HBM market share. The Tongluo site will accelerate Micron's production ramp and significant product shipments are expected from the existing line beginning in fiscal 2028, with the second facility adding capacity thereafter.

science.headline: Sourdough fermentation found to transform wheat fibers and enhance prebiotic benefits
science.description: Research from Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB), published in March 2026, found that sourdough fermentation transforms wheat dietary fibers called arabinoxylans in ways previously unknown. The transformation is driven primarily by wheat-native enzymes activated by the sourdough's acidic environment, which break large fiber molecules into smaller fragments. The research also identified specific bacteria — Lactococcus lactis creating buttery aromas and Limosilactobacillus fermentum producing mild sweetness — contributing to sourdough's distinctive flavour profile.
science.context: Arabinoxylans are the primary dietary fiber in wheat and play an important role in gut health and bread structure. Understanding their transformation during fermentation has implications for the food industry's ability to design breads with enhanced prebiotic properties, improved digestibility, and better texture. The findings also support the broader scientific interest in fermented foods as functional health products, particularly amid rising consumer demand for natural gut health solutions.
